author: sama
text: I think seed prices are often disconnected from reality. I just don't think it's the fault of founders.

author: sama
text: to make my own views clear: I would like to see less money chasing seed startups. I think it'd be better all around.

author: sama
text: 7) founder to me: "every investor says they provide more value than other investors and i should give them advisor shares. what do i do?"

author: sama
text: 6) and generally speaking, "value investing" is not the way to win in early-stage startup investing.  investing in the best companies is.

author: sama
text: 5) investors: if you don't like the price for a company, don't invest.  don't berate the founder.

author: sama
text: 4) founders make their own decisions about how much value they'll actually get from investors, and whether to give a discount for it

author: sama
text: 3) but there's not much we can do about market pricing--there are a lot of investors willing to pay high prices.

author: sama
text: 2) believe it or not, we really try to tell founders not to optimize for valuation.  most actually listen and don't take the higher offer.
